narrative.origin_story: Eleanor Vance is 51, runs a Series C agritech scale-up out of London with operations across East Africa, and has been a CEO for eleven of the last fifteen years.
narrative.manifesto:
The future is not announced. It is decided in small rooms by serious people, and announced when the deal closes.

By the time a market category is named in a public deck, the Global Leaders who shaped it have already deployed capital, formed partnerships, and tested the regulatory edges in the territories that matter. The category is named for the public. The Global Leaders are already deploying against the next one.

Visionnaire is the standing room those Global Leaders walk into.

We are not a luxury social house. We have learned the lesson [Soho House](https://www.sohohouse.com) taught the membership category: scale without density dilutes the room. We refuse the trade. Our ceiling is set by capacity of attention, not by capacity of dues.

We are not a peer advisory group. [TIGER 21](https://www.tiger21.com) and [YPO](https://www.ypo.org) are excellent at the format we adopt for some of our circles. They are not optimized for capital deployment as the defining act. We are.

We are not a public think tank. The [World Economic Forum](https://www.weforum.org) sets agendas in public. We set agendas in private and publish only the deals.

What Visionnaire is: a four-tier admission-gated circle of operating Global Leaders — founders past Series C, family office principals, institutional investors with frontier mandates, and the leaders of organizations whose decisions outlast their own tenure. A standing programmable surface — quarterly residencies in MirageZ markets, monthly closed circles, weekly strategic briefings, ProLab venture co-development, the annual summit. A defined deal velocity — a measured median of 47 days from a pre-seeded room to a signed term sheet across ProLab. And a published admission logic — operating scale, capital authority, frontier experience, and reference verification, with a curated rejection rate near 30%.

The room is small. The membership is named (privately to other members). The deals are real.

---
